verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. services-marketplace-cx.md:23 ("Resolved: the cap gates quote *issuance*, not acceptance") and :137 ("issuance of a *new* quote is what the ceiling blocks. Failure surfaces at issuance ('you're at capacity')") state a gate at issuance. 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:170 (DT-04) rejects option (a) and concludes "The design obligation is therefore not a gate but **legibility**", and 05.02.01:112 says "The ceiling binds *ordering* (05.01.07 D-03), not acceptance" with the at-ceiling seller told they went over rather than blocked. Ordering != issuance, so the two are not reconcilable by reading. 05.01.07 D-03 (:94) governs orderability only and 05.01.07 says nothing about quote issuance, so neither owner file supports the CX's issuance gate. Two normative statements about the same DT-04 resolution cannot both hold; a seller at capacity either can or cannot issue a quote.

Half the claim refuted, half survives. The Carried Terms table (05.02.01:37-58) was read in full: there is no recall/support-window row, and a domain-wide search for 'recall'/'support window' returns ZERO hits outside 05.03.06 itself — so nothing anywhere carries the term that 05.03.06:89 (D-03, 'bounded in both duration and count') requires, and 05.02.01:14/:35/:236 make an omission from that table normatively fatal. The trial-scope half is refuted: 'Milestone structure + tranches' is row :55 and D-17 (:246) routes a trial scope through milestones, so it is carried. Downgraded from blocking because 05.03.06 is [SURFACE] (:5) with its window length still open and owned (Q-04, User), so this is an unfinished feature's consequence rather than two normative statements colliding.

Quotes are accurate but the inference is not. D-13 (05.03.05:281) states a liability *cap*, never an obligation; a cap of GBP 400 over an obligation of zero is satisfied, not contradicted. DT-12 (:234) explicitly rejects making the seller cover the buyer's room and states the platform's job is 'to **warn before the loss**, not to reallocate it after', which is exactly what the :169 booking-time copy does ('your room deposit is not covered'). :84 ('Seller-fault, both models: zero') and D-20 (:288) then converge with DT-12 on a zero settlement leg. The 'date guarantee' (:170) is a negotiated contract term the seller priced, not the platform-imposed reverse kill fee D-20 forbids. Every reasonable reading converges on: seller pays nothing by default, cap bounds any declared instrument.

Quotes verified: 05.01.02:44 records rights posture at 'Exactly 1' under the column header 'Cardinality on a listing' (:35), while 05.01.01:183 (D-02) is 'per tier ... because tiers routinely differ' and 05.06.01:34 is 'two elections per tier'. The numbers cannot all be right, and nothing reconciles them — notably 05.01.02 DT-14 (:137) wrestled with exactly this tier-crossing problem for the craft axis and resolved it (primary + derived secondary, D-07 :170) while leaving the posture row untouched. Downgraded from blocking: the publish gate is not unimplementable, because 05.01.01:74 ('Publish blocked — election is per **tier**, not per listing') is explicit and no implementer would build a single listing-level field from a facet table. The live residual is what the posture facet indexes for a multi-posture listing.

The file states the arithmetic. 05.01.01:39 step 5 is '**Fee total** = subtotal + percentage add-ons' — a sum over a frozen subtotal, which is non-compounding and makes order irrelevant among percentage add-ons. That agrees with :38 ('applied to the subtotal') and with the model name 'percentage-of-subtotal' (:43). D-03's 'the order matters' (:184) refers to the pipeline order it names in the same clause (percentages after the subtotal; expenses outside the take-rate base), not to ordering among percentage add-ons. The 'incompatible notations' claim also fails: +50% and x1.5 are the same operation on a subtotal. Both worked figures land on GBP 4,000.

The finding's own evidence resolves it. The prose at 05.01.03:49 cites D-03/D-04/D-05 as its authority, and D-04 (:186) narrows currency and tax treatment to 'Every **cash** model' — so the decision layer, which is normative here, already carves zero-cash models out of the only two parameters that make no sense for them. Minimum (D-03, :185) and rounding (D-05, :187) are stated unqualified in both places, so there is no competing statement for an implementer to diverge from; a minimum percentage and a rounding rule on a percentage are expressible. Currency is also defaulted, not blocking ('Defaults to the seller's payout currency', :54), so no publish gate ever fires on it. Points-only listings are not made unpublishable by any reading.

Both quotes are verbatim, but the Happy Path line is a compressed restatement, not a competing rule. 05.01.07:32 specifies the mechanism in full and explicitly forecloses the alternative ('It is not a first-to-click free-for-all'), and the edge case at :52 operationalises it ('The freed-slot offer expires (Level-1 default: 24h) and passes to the next buyer in join order; the lapsed buyer keeps their original queue position'). Under sequential offering, 'notified in order; the first to convert takes the slot' is true and describes the same outcome. No competent implementer builds a simultaneous blast against an explicit prohibition plus a stated lapse-and-pass rule.

Quotes verified (05.01.07:17, :93 D-02, Q-01..Q-04 at :100-103), but the finding attacks the *rationale* rather than an ambiguity. D-02 is unambiguous — 'per human per craft' — so both implementers build per-craft ceilings with no aggregate cap and produce identical behaviour; nothing is invented. The 'one finite week' phrasing is justification prose contrasting per-human with per-listing (the harm 05.01.01:77 names: 'More listings don't add capacity'), not a competing rule. That the design may under-protect a multi-hyphenate is a product critique, not a specification divergence.

The release-detection dependency is carried, and the finding cites the tracking itself: 05.01.03:206 Q-07 is '[PREREQUISITE — blocking, promoted 2026-07-30] ... **Who detects the trigger and notifies**', owner Agent, target /create-prd-architecture, coordinate with 12 — and 05.02.03:97 Q-02 is explicitly paired to it as 'the same shape — an obligation the engagement cannot see ... needing something outside this domain to observe the event and reach back'. Any Delayed-embargo surfacing inherits that resolution. Independently, D-05 (05.02.02:115) is date-driven: election requires a backstop *date*, expiry fires on a date, and the credit converts to Sealed rather than auto-publishing — a mechanism computable without observing a release.

Quote verified verbatim at 05.02.03:48, and it carries '[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]' — a marker with a named stage, in the kit's standard shape, on a file whose own status line (05.02.03:5) is [SURFACE] and whose parent index (05.02-index:20) records it as [SURFACE] with 3 hypotheses. The file has not had a deepening pass, so a deferral to that pass is coherent tracking, not an orphan. The 'target already declared complete' argument rests on services-marketplace-cx.md:5, which is the metadata defect raised separately as #017; it does not convert this row into an untracked gap.

The cited cell (05.04.01:56) does not close the question — it states an interim value and in the same sentence names the owner and forbids itself from deciding: 'per 05.01.06 Q-02, **which owns this question**. This feature inherits whatever that resolves to and **must not answer it independently**', restated at :191. 05.01.06:105 confirms Q-02 is open with owner User and target 'Step 5 deepening'. This is the same interim-stance-plus-owner pattern the tree uses elsewhere (e.g. 05.01.07:54, 'Level-1 interim ... Final default value is user-owned'). Owner and target both present, tracking well-formed.

The distinction is owned by the sibling that owns the commit, and 05.04.01 routes there explicitly. 05.06.03:236 (D-06) is unqualified: '**The ledger is in the commit; the payment rail is not.** A failed payout never unwinds a rights transfer — it is a debt the platform owes the seller ... This is what makes withholding a suspended seller's money possible without corrupting a title', and :139 applies it to the analogous suspended-seller case. 05.04.01:192 names 05.06.03 as 'one event, two sides ... The rights leg'. The literal reading the finding proposes (money leg = escrow release deferred, all-three-or-none broken) is foreclosed by the very decision the transfer owner states; the wording at :119 is terse, not divergent.

All quotes verified, but the behaviour is decided rather than ambiguous. D-02 (index:46, 05.04.02:104) gates delivery on a file that *fails* QC; D-05 (05.04.02:107) governs the disjoint case where the engine is *unavailable* — 'fail open with a visible flag', with a stated rationale. These are different antecedents and both hold simultaneously. 05.04.01:183 records the consequence and calls it '**deliberate**'. Two implementers converge: publish, flag visibly, run the clock. The residual is an acknowledged product risk, not a forced invention — and DT-01 / sub-domain Q-01 (index:54, owner User, /create-prd-security) already owns the 'rights by silence' exposure this scenario turns on.

Verified verbatim at 05.05-multi-party-supply-cx.md:73 and services-marketplace-cx.md:104, both bare '[PENDING]' — no owner, no stage, no target. Confirmed by reading the full question lists: 05.05 index Q-01..Q-03 (:53-55) are credit counterparty, margin disclosure and entity-as-seller; 05.05.02 Q-01..Q-03 (:102-104) are margin, roster visibility and off-platform players. None covers the freeze. The only stated freeze rule in the domain is whole-escrow (05.04.01:133, 'Escrow frozen ... Nothing transfers while frozen'), which the CX itself declares wrong for this case, and 05.05.02 D-02 (:94) asserts atomic settlement from one release with no freeze semantics. The tracking is malformed and the behaviour must be invented.

The marker at 05.06.02:62 is bare as quoted, but the default falls out of the file's own decisions rather than requiring invention. D-01 (:112) forbids conflating master points with publishing share ('never one "points" field'), which rules out the 'follows the composition' branch outright, and D-04 (:115) binds the election to '**the recording's** aggregate allocation (09)' — a participation is attached to the recording it was validated against, so a later re-recording is a different asset with its own allocation. Both implementers land in the same place. What remains is a product-scope question (should a quote carry a re-record restriction term), not a divergence in buildable behaviour.

Verified verbatim at 05.07-custodial-physical-services-cx.md:41 — 'Both need a defined precedence; `[PENDING]`', bare, with no owner and no stage. Question lists read in full: 05.07.01 Q-01..Q-04 (return shipping, abandoned item, diagnostic fee, declined-revision return state), 05.07.03 Q-01..Q-04 (insurance, declared value, devaluation warning, orphaned item), 05.07 index Q-01..Q-03 (insurance, gear registry, in-scope) — none covers either race. 05.07.03's decisions do not settle it either: D-01 gives per-handoff condition records and D-04 makes the approved estimate the measure, but neither says whether a damage record may attach while the job state still reads In Progress, or which of a revision and a return-in-flight wins. Comparable races elsewhere carry explicit precedence decisions (05.03.05 D-16, 05.05.01 D-05, 05.04.01 D-04).

Verified and, if anything, understated. services-marketplace-index.md:5 is [BREADTH] with all seven children marked `[BREADTH]` (:33-39) and a header still asserting 32 leaf features 'all `[SURFACE]`' (:29), while services-marketplace-cx.md:5 claims '[DEEP] — 7 sub-domains, **deepening pass complete**'. A full status sweep of the tree gives 11 [DEEP], 13 [PARTIAL], 10 [SURFACE] leaves — 21 of 32 not deep, not the 15 the finding claims. The live consequence is real and larger than stated: 39 lines across the domain defer to 'Step 5 deepening' / 'Step 5 Must-depth', including owner-assigned open questions (05.01.06 Q-02, 05.01.07 Q-02/Q-03, 05.03.06 Q-03/Q-04, 05.05.03 Q-03/Q-04, 05.07.01 Q-03/Q-04), all pointing at a pass one file declares finished.
